# arcane_api_resource (Resource)

Manages an Arcane API object from a YAML manifest. The provider adds the `terraform.arcane.pubg.io/managed-by: terraform` label when it creates or updates the object, unless the manifest sets that label. When the label is removed on the server, the next plan shows it as drift and the next apply puts it back. It does not appear in `desired_object`. The provider keeps managing the label even when `ignore_differences` selects it or a field above it, such as `metadata.labels`.

`manifest` is always sensitive, so plans show manifest changes in `desired_object`, where secret fields read `******`. Secret fields are the fields the API server reports as encrypted through API discovery, plus the fields `sensitive_fields` selects for secret fields the server does not know about. `live_object` is what the server actually stores, and `desired_object` is what you wrote.

~> Terraform does not tell the provider which values are sensitive. A sensitive value placed in a field that the server does not report as encrypted shows in plain text in `desired_object` unless `sensitive_fields` selects that field. Provider versions without `desired_object` hid the whole manifest, so check existing configurations for such values before upgrading.

For an airdrop `Secret`, write values under `data` instead of `stringData`. The server does not store `stringData`, so it never appears in `live_object`, only in `desired_object`.

For a kind with encrypted fields, the provider reads their plaintext through the `<plural>/reveal` subresource, so the token needs `get` on `<plural>/reveal`. Only kinds with encrypted fields need it. Without it, encrypted values are not compared, so they never trigger an update, and an update fails when `ignore_differences` selects an encrypted field. A changed encrypted field shows in the `live_object` diff as `"******" -> (known after apply)`.

Drift shows in the plan as a field-level diff of `live_object`. Fields only the server has are drift too, and apply removes them. To keep such a field, select it with `ignore_differences`, for example `managed_fields_managers = ["qa-quick-access-web"]`. The plan sends a `PUT` with `?dryRun=All` to compare the server's result with its object, so the token needs `update` on the kind, even for a plan. The API server must honor `dryRun`. A server that ignores it stores the plan's `PUT`. The provider detects that from the response's `resourceVersion` and warns, but cannot undo the write. Apply sends the same dry run before each `PUT`. When the object changed on the server after the plan so that the update would store values other than the planned ones, for example when someone edits a field `ignore_differences` selects, apply stops without updating the object and asks you to plan again.

An update that needs no `PUT` does not wait, and with `wait` a `PUT` plans the whole `live_object` as unknown. Without `wait`, a `PUT` plans `live_object` from the dry run, and only changed secret fields are unknown. It plans the fields `ignore_differences` selects with their values in the state. `live_object` leaves out `metadata.resourceVersion`, `metadata.updateTimestamp` and `metadata.generation`, which the server sets on writes, so they never show in a plan. `data.arcane_api_resource` returns them.

After upgrading from a provider version without `desired_object`, the first plan fills it during refresh. A plan with `-refresh=false` skips that, so it can show one in-place update with no other change.

## Upgrading

Earlier provider versions stored the server's object in `object` as a JSON string and had a `drift` attribute. `object` was renamed to `live_object`, and it is an object value now. After upgrading:

- Replace `yamldecode(arcane_api_resource.x.object)` and `jsondecode(arcane_api_resource.x.object)` with direct references. For values you wrote in the manifest, use `arcane_api_resource.x.desired_object.<path>`, such as `arcane_api_resource.x.desired_object.metadata.name`, which is known at plan time. For values the server sets, use `arcane_api_resource.x.live_object.<path>`, such as `arcane_api_resource.x.live_object.metadata.uid`.
- The `drift` attribute is removed. Drift shows in the plan as the diff of `live_object`.
- `live_object` no longer has `metadata.resourceVersion`, `metadata.updateTimestamp` and `metadata.generation`. To read them, or `metadata.managedFields`, use `data.arcane_api_resource`, whose `object` keeps every field the server returns.
- `data.arcane_api_resources` returns `objects` as a list (tuple) of objects instead of YAML strings, and `data.arcane_api_resource`, `arcane_command` and `data.arcane_command` return `object` as an object value. Reference their fields directly, too.
- Every field `ignore_differences` selects now keeps the server's value on update, like `ignore_changes` of the `lifecycle` block. The first plan after upgrading shows an update that only rewrites the `terraform.arcane.pubg.io/ignore-differences` annotation for every resource with `ignore_differences`, unless its manifest sets that annotation.
- A block that selects an encrypted field now needs `get` on `<plural>/reveal` for every update. Without it, the update fails with `Failed to reveal ignored encrypted fields`.
- The plan sends a dry run, so the token that runs `terraform plan` needs `update` on each kind.
- The first plan after upgrading can show fields that other tools added on the server as drift. Check the `live_object` diff before applying, and keep such fields with `ignore_differences`.

After upgrading from v1.0.0, the first plan shows an update that only rewrites the `terraform.arcane.pubg.io/ignore-differences` annotation for every resource with `ignore_differences`, unless its manifest sets that annotation.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Cluster scoped api resource
resource "arcane_api_resource" "test" {
  manifest = <<-YAML
apiVersion: bluechip.pubg.io/v1
kind: Vendor
metadata:
  name: test-vendor
spec:
  codeName: NCP
  displayName: test
  shortName: dd
  regions:
  - AP-NORTHEAST-222
YAML
}

# Namespace scoped api resource
resource "arcane_api_resource" "test_namespaced" {
  manifest = <<-YAML
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.arcane.pubg.io/v1
kind: Role
metadata:
  annotations:
    foo: bar
  labels: {}
  name: arcane-provider-test
  namespace: default
rules:
- apiGroups:
  - bluechip.pubg.io
  resources:
  - ingameimages
  verbs:
  - '*'
- apiGroups:
  - ""
  resources:
  - namespaces
  verbs:
  - get
  - create
YAML
}

# Leave fields that a controller changes alone, and wait until the object is ready
resource "arcane_api_resource" "with_wait" {
  # An autoscaler changes replicas, so an update keeps the server's value.
  ignore_differences {
    json_pointers = ["/spec/replicas"]
  }

  # Keep a sidecar a controller adds, and the fields that controller owns.
  ignore_differences {
    jq_path_expressions     = [".spec.containers[] | select(.name == \"sidecar\")"]
    managed_fields_managers = ["worker-controller"]
  }

  manifest = <<-YAML
apiVersion: example.pubg.io/v1
kind: Worker
metadata:
  name: worker
  namespace: default
spec:
  replicas: 2
YAML

  wait {
    condition {
      type   = "Ready"
      status = "True"
    }
    field {
      jq_path_expression = ".status.phase"
      value              = "Running"
    }
  }
}

data "vault_kv_secret_v2" "db" {
  mount = "kv"
  name  = "qa/db"
}

# Secret values from Vault. manifest is always sensitive, so a plan shows its changes in desired_object, where encrypted fields read "******".
# Write values under data, not stringData: the server does not store stringData, so it never appears in live_object, only in desired_object.
resource "arcane_api_resource" "db_secret" {
  manifest = <<-YAML
apiVersion: workload.airdrop.pubg.io/v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: db
  namespace: qa
data:
  password: ${base64encode(data.vault_kv_secret_v2.db.data["password"])}
YAML
}

# Mark secret fields the API server does not report as encrypted
resource "arcane_api_resource" "with_sensitive_fields" {
  sensitive_fields {
    json_pointers       = ["/spec/credentials"]
    jq_path_expressions = [".spec.items[] | select(.type == \"slack\") | .token"]
  }

  manifest = <<-YAML
apiVersion: example.pubg.io/v1
kind: Connector
metadata:
  name: connector
  namespace: default
spec:
  items:
  - type: slack
    token: ${data.vault_kv_secret_v2.db.data["token"]}
  credentials:
    user: app
    password: ${data.vault_kv_secret_v2.db.data["password"]}
YAML
}

# Reference the manifest as an object, with secret fields masked
output "db_secret_labels" {
  value = arcane_api_resource.db_secret.desired_object.metadata
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `manifest` (String, Sensitive) YAML manifest of the resource. Always sensitive; see desired_object for its changes. Changing apiVersion, kind, metadata.name or metadata.namespace forces a new resource.

### Optional

- `ignore_differences` (Block List) Fields to leave out of drift detection and to keep at the server's values on update, like `ignore_changes` of the `lifecycle` block, or `ignoreDifferences` of an Argo CD Application with the `RespectIgnoreDifferences=true` sync option. Each block selects fields with `json_pointers`, `jq_path_expressions` and `managed_fields_managers`, and must select at least one. The provider resolves the selectors on the manifest and on the server's object separately, removes the selected fields from each, and compares what remains. So a field only the server has, such as a sidecar container a controller adds, can be left out without matching array indexes. A selected field also covers every field under it, and a map left empty by the removal is removed too, so a map holding only ignored keys is not drift when the server does not have it. A jq expression that fails to evaluate on an object selects nothing on that object. A manager whose entries in `metadata.managedFields` cannot be parsed selects nothing. A selector that resolves to the whole object, such as the jq expression `.`, is ignored. Create sends the manifest as written. An update sends the server's values of the selected fields instead of the manifest values, and leaves out a selected field the server does not have. A selected array element only the server has, such as a sidecar container, stays at its index on the server, and the manifest's other elements fill the remaining places in order. For a JSON Pointer or a jq expression, such an element inside another array element is left out, because its index on the server may point at a different element of the manifest. A field inside an element is matched to the manifest's element by the same JSON Pointer, by the keys in `metadata.managedFields` for a manager, and by the order of results for a jq expression. When a jq expression selects fields on both the manifest and the server's object, and on either of them selects several fields that differ only in array indexes, such as `.spec.containers[].resources`, the update skips the expression and sends the manifest values for its fields, with a warning. So a jq expression should select one element, as `select(.name == "app")` does. A field inside an element the manifest does not have is left out, and so is an element a manager owns in an array the manifest's element does not have. When a selected field is an encrypted field, the provider reads its value through the `<plural>/reveal` subresource. The plan shows the selected fields with their values in the state. When one of them changes on the server between plan and apply, apply stops without updating the object and asks you to plan again. When nothing else differs and the manifest is unchanged, the provider does not update the object, so changes on the server limited to ignored fields stay. So that people reading the object can see which fields Terraform leaves alone, the provider writes the blocks as a JSON array to the `terraform.arcane.pubg.io/ignore-differences` annotation, unless the manifest sets that annotation. Like the managed-by label, the annotation is put back on the next apply when it is removed on the server, is removed when no block is left, and does not appear in `desired_object`. The provider always compares the managed-by label and this annotation, even when a block selects them or a field above them. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--ignore_differences))
- `sensitive_fields` (Block, Optional) Fields to treat as secret in addition to the fields the API server reports as encrypted. A selected field also covers every field under it. Their values read `******` in `desired_object` and `live_object`. The provider runs the jq expressions on the manifest at plan time to compute `desired_object`, and on the server's object to compute `live_object`. When a jq expression fails to evaluate on an object, every value of that object except `apiVersion`, `kind`, `metadata.name` and `metadata.namespace` reads `******`, with a warning. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--sensitive_fields))
- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))
- `wait` (Block, Optional) Conditions to wait for after the object is created or updated, bounded by the create and update timeouts. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--wait))

### Read-Only

- `desired_object` (Dynamic) The manifest as written, as an object value, with secret fields replaced by `******`. Secret fields are the encrypted fields reported by API discovery plus the fields `sensitive_fields` selects. Other fields show in plain text even when their value comes from a sensitive variable or attribute. Computed at plan time, and unknown while the manifest is unknown. Reference fields such as `desired_object.spec.replicas`.
- `id` (String) API path of the resource
- `live_object` (Dynamic) Resource object returned by the API server, as an object value. It is what the server actually stores, without `metadata.managedFields`, `metadata.resourceVersion`, `metadata.updateTimestamp` and `metadata.generation`. The server returns encrypted fields as `******`, and the provider also replaces the fields `sensitive_fields` selects with `******`. Without `wait`, fields of subresources such as `status` are updated on the next refresh. Reference fields such as `live_object.metadata.uid`.

<a id="nestedblock--ignore_differences"></a>
### Nested Schema for `ignore_differences`

Optional:

- `jq_path_expressions` (List of String) jq path expressions that select the fields, such as `.spec.integrations[] | select(.type == "slack") | .token`. Each expression has one second to evaluate.
- `json_pointers` (List of String) JSON Pointers (RFC 6901) of the fields, such as `/data/password`. A pointer to a field the object does not have selects nothing.
- `managed_fields_managers` (List of String) Field manager names, such as `pet-controller`. The fields a manager owns in `metadata.managedFields` of the server's object are removed from both the manifest and the server's object. Unlike Argo CD, which ignores only owned fields that both sides have, an owned field is ignored even when the manifest leaves it out. An array element or map that a manager owns together with fields under it, such as a sidecar container a controller adds, is ignored whole when only the server has it. When the manifest has it too, only the fields under it that the manager owns are ignored. An update sends the server's values of owned fields, and the API server keeps the ownership of a field whose value an update leaves unchanged. When an update sends a different value for an owned field, such as a field removed from a manifest element or a field of a skipped jq expression, the ownership moves to the provider, and the field is not ignored again until that manager writes it.


<a id="nestedblock--sensitive_fields"></a>
### Nested Schema for `sensitive_fields`

Optional:

- `jq_path_expressions` (List of String) jq path expressions that select the fields, such as `.spec.integrations[] | select(.type == "slack") | .token`. Each expression has one second to evaluate.
- `json_pointers` (List of String) JSON Pointers (RFC 6901) of the fields, such as `/data/password`. A pointer to a field the object does not have selects nothing.


<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `delete` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Setting a timeout for a Delete operation is only applicable if changes are saved into state before the destroy operation occurs.
- `read` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Read operations occur during any refresh or planning operation when refresh is enabled.
- `update` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).


<a id="nestedblock--wait"></a>
### Nested Schema for `wait`

Optional:

- `condition` (Block List) An entry in `status.conditions` that must have this status. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--wait--condition))
- `field` (Block List) A field that must have this value. Values that are not strings are compared as JSON. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--wait--field))

<a id="nestedblock--wait--condition"></a>
### Nested Schema for `wait.condition`

Required:

- `status` (String) Condition status, such as True.
- `type` (String) Condition type, such as Ready.


<a id="nestedblock--wait--field"></a>
### Nested Schema for `wait.field`

Required:

- `value` (String) Value to wait for.

Optional:

- `jq_path_expression` (String) jq expression that selects the fields, such as .status.replicas[].ready. Every selected field must have the value. Exactly one of `json_pointer` and `jq_path_expression`.
- `json_pointer` (String) JSON Pointer to the field, such as /status/phase. Exactly one of `json_pointer` and `jq_path_expression`.
- `value_type` (String) How to compare the value: eq (default) or regex.
